incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — p99 streaming latency spike for tenant MarlinPay. SLO breached (p99 > 5s) on /v1/chat/stream. Auto-page sent to @oncall-alex
oncall-alex: I’m on it. quick summary?
sre-jordan: seeing a big tail-event for MarlinPay only. p95 ~350ms, p99 ~7.2s, streaming stalls and partial responses (clients reconnecting). Error rate small (~0.6%) but retries causing amplification. Concurrent live sessions from MarlinPay jumped from ~2k -> ~12k over last 10m.
eng-runtime-sam: any obvious infra failures? nodes OOMing? pod restarts?
sre-jordan: no pod restarts, but memory pressure on worker nodes. KV cache size per model worker increased ~3x for the tenant. Observed many long prefixes (~10k tokens) and repeated concurrent sessions reusing similar long prefixes -> KV cache thrash.
ml-ops-lee: model logs show stalls at generation step: 
```
[EPOCH] token-gen blocked waiting for KV_CACHE_LOCK (200ms)
[PERF] KV cache entries 1.8M -> 5.6M in 8m for tenant MarlinPay
[QUEUE] per-request queued time spiked to 600ms
```

oncall-alex: tagged eng-runtime and ml-ops. Immediate mitigations we can try?
eng-runtime-sam: immediate mitigations I can run: 1) route MarlinPay to latency-optimized model shard pool (less KV-heavy variant), 2) enable tenant-level request-throttling to cap burst concurrency, 3) bump per-worker eviction aggressive threshold to free KV memory. I’ll enact 1+2 first.
sre-jordan: +1. Also we can temporarily increase dedicated capacity for that tenant if autoscaler lagging.
cs-maya: I’ve DM'd MarlinPay support lead (kevin@marlinpay) — telling them we’re investigating and mitigation in progress. Asking them to pause non-critical bulk sessions.
oncall-alex: go ahead, Sam please apply mitigations and post commands you run. Keep this thread as the handoff log.
eng-runtime-sam: running route update now: 
```
# route MarlinPay traffic to latency-optimized pool
rwctl routing set --tenant marlinpay --policy latency-first --model rwd-latopt-3b
# apply tenant throttle: max-concurrent-sessions 3000
rwctl tenant update marlinpay --max-concurrency=3000
```
deploy-bot: :rocket: route update submitted, rollout id 8a3f. Canary started on 5% of sessions.
eng-runtime-sam: increasing eviction aggressiveness for KV cache on pool nodes:
```
kubectl exec -n runtime svc/cache-config -- curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/config -d '{"kv_eviction_pct":30}'
```
ml-ops-lee: watch model quality — routing to smaller model may reduce output fidelity. Running evaluation on 50 sample prompts from MarlinPay to confirm acceptable.
sre-jordan: metrics after 2m of mitigations: p99 (canary) ~1.1s, p95 ~320ms, concurrent sessions offloaded. No new OOMs.
cs-maya: MarlinPay support acknowledges mitigation and paused some non-critical runs. They report partial improvement on their side.
oncall-alex: handing to eng-runtime-sam for deeper investigation. I’ll remain on the channel until full resolution. Handoff note: escalation to SEs if QoL regressions.
eng-runtime-sam: taking over for deeper dive. Initial hypothesis: MarlinPay's client app opened many near-simultaneous long-lived streaming sessions that share long prompt prefixes causing exponential KV growth and synchronous lock contention when filling KV caches. Two-pronged remediation plan: short-term (we applied routing + throttling + eviction); medium-term (apply prefix compression, tenant-level cache quotas, and smarter KV sharding), long-term (adaptive throttling + prompt-length-based routing).
sre-jordan: tracing capture links: https://internal.telemetry/trace/8a3f-marlinpay (added logs + flamegraphs).
eng-runtime-sam: follow-ups created: RUNTIME-456 (prefix compression prototype), RUNTIME-457 (tenant cache quotas + metrics), SRE-1123 (autoscaler responsiveness tuning). I’ll attach perf traces and KV profiles.
ml-ops-lee: evaluation results: fidelity drop minimal for most prompts; 3/50 cases flagged — will send counterexamples.
oncall-alex: status update: mitigations holding at last check. p99 for full tenant now ~1.3s (still above our ideal but under breach threshold). Keeping page open.
eng-runtime-sam: next steps: collect full heap dumps from 3 affected worker nodes after peak subsides, run offline KV eviction simulation, coordinate with MarlinPay engineers on client-side connection patterns. I’ll own postmortem.
cs-maya: I confirmed MarlinPay wants a short post-incident note and a follow-up tech sync tomorrow.
oncall-alex: thanks all. If anything regresses, escalate to SRE lead. Closing on-call handoff to Sam at +10m. :bow:
